RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Tuesday,  the March 11, 2008/Phalguna 21, 1929 (Saka)
————
(Ministries: Civil Aviation; Corporate Affairs; Culture; Finance; Heavy
Industries and Public Enterprises; Petroleum and Natural Gas;
Tourism; Water Resources)
Total number of questions — 20
49
Crime against tourists
†*161. SHRIMATI PREMA
CARIAPPA:
SHRIMATI SUSHMA
SWARAJ:
Will the Minister of TOURISM be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government has taken note
of increasing cases of crime against tourists
at tourist centres;
(b) whether Government has under its
consideration a mechanism to prevent
crimes against tourists; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?
Illegal constructions near Humayun
Tomb
*162. SHRIMATI HEMA MALINI:
Will the Minister of CULTURE be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that some illegal
constructions have come up through nexus
between Archaeological Survey of India
(ASI) officials and local police near
Humayun Tomb, Delhi;
(b) if so, whether Government is
considering to apply some preventive
measures;
(c) whether Government has been able
to unearth the nexus between officials of
ASI and the local police; and
(d) if so, the details of the steps
Government proposes to take against those
erring officials?
Full utilisation of runways
at airports
*163. PROF. ALKA BALRAM
KSHATRIYA:
SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA:
Will the Minister of CIVIL  A VIATION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Directorate General of
Civil Aviation plans to maximize utilization
of runways at major airports around the
country;
(b) if so, whether proper infrastructure
is available at major airports to make
utilization of runways;
(c) if so, the details thereof; and
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

50
(d) to what extent the major airports
would be modernized to have full utilization
of runways?
Committee on merger of Public
Sector Banks
†*164. MISS ANUSUIYA UIKEY: Will
the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to
state:
(a) whether any Committee had been
constituted by Government to suggest the
merging of Public Sector Banks;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether the report has been
submitted to Government by the
Committee;
(d) if so, when was it submitted;
(e) the names of banks proposed to be
merged on the basis of this report and the
reasons of this merging; and
(f) by when the procedure for merging
would be completed and what would be its
benefits?
Civil aviation agreement between
India and Pakistan
†*165. MS. SUSHILA TIRIYA:
SHRI MOTILAL VORA:
Will the Minister of CIVIL  A VIATION
be pleased to state:
(a) the matters on which discussions
were held recently between Civil Aviation
officials of India and Pakistan;
(b) whether a decision was taken to
increase the number of flights from 12 to
28 in a week and to link Chennai and
Islamabad by air route to boost mutual
relationship among the citizens of India and
Pakistan in this mutual talk;
(c) the names of airlines which have
applied for providing flights to Pakistan;
and
(d) the names of airlines permitted to
ply between India and Pakistan and the
criteria adopted for the same?
Derivatives trading by Indian banks
*166. SHRI RAJEEV CHANDRA-
SEKHAR: Will the Minister of FINANCE
be pleased to state:
(a) the quantum of derivatives trading
and exposure on Indian stock market by
Indian banks with their own capital during
the last three years ending 31 December,
2007, year-wise and bank-wise; and
(b) what systematic safeguards are in
place to prevent the recurrence of any large
scale losses arising from derivatives trading
like the one recently reported in France by
Societe Generale?
Reduction of bulk LPG supply by
RIL to IOC
*167. SHRI MOHAMMED AMIN:
SHRI TAPAN KUMAR SEN:
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM
AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to
state:
(a) whether recent LPG shortage in the
country was also due to reduction in bulk
LPG supplies by Reliance Industries Ltd.
(RIL) in the month of January, 2008 to
Indian Oil Corporation (IOC) and other
public sector oil marketing companies;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether there are any penal
provisions in case of such abrupt reduction
of supply by RIL;
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

51
(d) if so, the details thereof; and
(e) if not, the reasons therefor?
Preferential allotments by companies
*168. MS. MABEL REBELLO: Will
the Minister of CORPORATE AFFAIRS
be pleased to state:
(a) how many companies have made
preferential allotments either to promoters
or other private groups during the last three
years;
(b) how many companies have sought
shareholders' approval for such preferential
allotments through postal ballot mechanism
and through general body meeting;
(c) whether Government is
contemplating to stop this method of
preferential allotment to promoters through
postal allotment as it hurts the small
investors whose value of share gets diluted;
(d) whether Government has any plans
to do so; and
(e) if so, by when;  and if not, the reasons
therefor?
Wages of ONGC workers
*169. SHRI PRAVEEN RASHTRA-
PAL: Will the Minister of PETROLEUM
AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to
state:
(a) the details of minimum wages paid
by Oil and Natural Gas Corporation
(ONGC) to workmen employed directly
by the Corporation as on 31 March, 2007;
(b) the details of minimum wages paid
to workers, casual workers, employed
through contractors as on 31 March, 2007;
(c) the details of various contractors
registered with ONGC on various assets
of ONGC in Gujarat; and
(d) the details of facilities, in addition
to wages, provided to above workers in
Gujarat region?
Purchasing of Government Securities
Bonds by Co-operative Banks
*170. SHRI S.S. AHLUWALIA: Will
the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Co-operative Banks have
been purchasing Government Securities
Bonds (G-Secs) largely through security
brokers;
(b) if so, the details of mechanism
approved/prescribed for investments by
Co-operative Banks in G-Secs indicating
mechanism dedicated to overseeing the
proceedings of dealing in G-Secs by Co-
operative Banks;
(c) whether it is a fact that instances of
several Co-operative Banks in Gujarat,
Orissa and other States, which have duly
paid for purchase of G-Secs to their assigned
brokers but are yet to receive delivery of
the Securities from brokers, have been
detected recently;
(d) if so, the details thereof; and
(e) the action taken; if any, in each
instance?
Import of SKO
*171. SHRI KESHUBHAI S. PA TEL:
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND
NATURAL GAS be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
has changed the EXIM Policy of import of
Superior Kerosene Oil (SKO) by parallel
markets;

52
(b) if so, whether Government is aware
that due to change of policy, the needy
bulk customers and other customers are
facing difficulty in getting free sale SKO
while it is easily available in the open
market;
(c) if so, whether there is any proposal
for separate marketing channel of parallel
marketeers in the State of Gujarat; and
(d) if so, the status of the proposal?
Shifting of 'Indira Gandhi Flying
Academy'
†*172. SHRI MOTILAL VORA:
SHRI SATYA VRAT
CHATURVEDI:
Will the Minister of CIVIL  A VIATION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that 'Indira Gandhi
Flying Academy' was set up at Fursatganj,
Rai Bareilly by the former Prime Minister
Shri Rajiv Gandhi;
(b) whether it is also a fact that this
Flying Academy has been shifted from
Fursatganj to Gondia (Maharashtra); and
(c) if so, the reasons therefor?
Loans advanced to farmers in Andhra
Pradesh
*173. SHRIMA TI N.P. DURGA: Will
the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
has surpassed the target of farm loans of
Rs. 1.72 lakh crore and achieved an
unprecedented Rs. 1.75 lakh crore;
(b) if so, the details of loan disbursed in
Andhra Pradesh;
(c) whether it is also a fact that
Government has now set a target of
disbursing Rs. 2.35 lakh crore to farmers;
(d) if so, the details thereof;
(e) whether any target has been set for
Andhra Pradesh; and
(f) if so, the details thereof?
Updation of websites of airports
*174. SHRI MAHENDRA MOHAN:
Will the Minister of CIVIL  A VIA TION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that official
websites of the Indian Airports are way
behind their international counterparts;
(b) whether it is also a fact that these
sites offer no information on flight status,
facilities at airports or tourist guide to their
cities;
(c) whether Government is aware that
it has been around eighteen months since
the GMR-led consortium, Delhi
International Airport Ltd. (DIAL), was
awarded the contract for the modernization
of Delhi Airport; and
(d) if so, whether Government would
like to fix the responsibilities and up-date
the websites too?
Promotion of village tourism
*175. MS. PRAMILA BOHIDAR:
SHRI B.J. PANDA:
Will the Minister of TOURISM be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government has identified
fifteen rural locations for promotion of
village tourism;
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

53
(b) if so, the details thereof, inter-alia,
indicating the rural locations that have been
identified in Orissa;
(c) how far tourism has picked up in
such locations after its launch; and
(d) what is the mode of funding on
infrastructure development in such
identified rural locations?
Bids for Natural Gas in Gujarat
*176. SHRI VIJAYKUMAR RUPANI:
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND
NATURAL GAS be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Panna Mukta
Tapti (PMT)  Joint Venture partners
invited the bids for sale of natural gas up to
4 Million Standard Cubic Meter per day
(MMSCMD) from 1 April, 2006 from
various companies;
(b) whether it is also a fact that Gujarat
State Petroleum Corporation Ltd. (GSPCL)
offered the highest price for gas amongst
the bidders;
(c) whether Government of Gujarat has
made any representation to Centre to
follow the rules of tender and offer gas to
GSPCL since their bid was the highest; and
(d) what is the reaction of the Central
Government to the representation?
Performance of public and private
sector oil companies
*177. SHRI TAPAN KUMAR SEN:
SHRI PRASANTA
CHATTERJEE:
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM
AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to
state:
(a) the gross refining margins of public
and private sector oil refineries, company-
wise during 2005-06, 2006-07 and 3rd
quarter of 2007-08;
(b) the net profit earned by Public
Sector Oil Marketing Companies and
Reliance Petroleum during 3rd quarter of
2006-07 and 2007-08;
(c) the total quantity of petroleum
products exported by public and private
sector oil companies; and
(d) the amount of concession/exemption
including Sales-Tax deferment, extended to
the above companies for export?
Dividend declared by Public Sector
Oil and Gas Companies
†*178. DR. MURLI MANOHAR
JOSHI:
SHRI RAJ MOHINDER
SINGH MAJITHA:
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM
AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that a number of
public sector organizations working in
petroleum industry have declared dividend
for their share holders for the years
2005-06, 2006-07 and upto December in
2007-08;
(b) if so, the names of such companies
(organizations); and
(c) the dividend decided to be paid to
the share holders by each of these
companies during the above period?
Linking of rivers
†*179. SHRIMATI MAYA SINGH:
Will the Minister of W ATER RESOURCES
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government has formulated
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

54
any scheme to avoid drought and flood by
linking various rivers of the country;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) the details of the rivers of Madhya
Pradesh which are proposed to be linked;
and
(d) by when the work is likely to be
started in this regard?
Supply of cooking gas in Goa
*180. SHRI SHANT ARAM
LAXMAN NAIK: Will the Minister of
PETROLEUM AND NA TURAL GAS be
pleased to state:
N
EW DELHI; V . K. AGNIHOTRI,
The 5th March, 2008 Secretary-General.
Phalguna 15, 1929 (Saka)
(a) the quantity of cooking gas sold by
various companies in Goa per month;
(b) the total cost price in actual of the
quantity sold;
(c) the total amount of subsidy
component on the gas sold in Goa;
(d) whether there is any proposal to
supply cooking gas in Goa; and
(e) if so, the details thereof?

I N D E X
(Ministry-wise)
Civil Aviation : 163, 165, 172, 174,
Corporate Affairs : 168,
Culture : 162,
Finance : 164, 166, 170, 173,
Heavy Industries and Public
Enterprises :—
Petroleum and Natural Gas : 167, 169, 171, 176, 177, 178, 180,
Tourism : 161, 175,
Water Resources : 179.
55
